evidence_note: The frozen trend deterioration appears under both legacy arithmetic excess and reconstructed NAV-difference semantics; metric redefinition does not explain the collapse.
Risk-free returns are used for risk-adjusted summaries, not the primary benchmark-relative selection objective or net-excess-NAV effect metric.

The publication-standard result is already negative on the exact frozen seven evaluation periods. Extending to the full 24-fold publication sample raises, rather than causes the loss of, mean performance.

Applying the Norgate 2026-07-20 constituent set retrospectively changes the same-vendor, same-period trend result from negative to strongly positive. This demonstrates a major survivorship-membership effect. The publication cost framework is unchanged, although liquidity-tier assignments may change endogenously because the membership universe itself changes.
Replacing XJOA with STW in both formation selection and evaluation changes mean performance only marginally, leaves positive-fold incidence unchanged, and changes parameter selection in no folds.

Removing all transaction costs improves mean performance but leaves it negative and leaves positive-fold incidence at 1/7. Costs are therefore a modest contributor, not an explanation for the sign reversal.

The frozen Yahoo current-constituent set could not be reconciled one-for-one to the Norgate panel without unsupported identity substitutions. Vendor/security coverage therefore remains unresolved and is not attributed to the point-in-time membership ablation.
